sampling_model.design: A deterministic partition into exactly \(B\) positive batches. Before outcomes are generated, each count rule is a Borel map \(q_b:(\mathsf H_{b-1},\mathcal G_{b-1})\to(\mathbb Z,2^{\mathbb Z})\). Evaluating it at the canonical prefix gives the \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\)-measurable count \(Q_b=q_b(O^{(b-1)})\), after which the batch is completely randomized conditional on \(Q_b\).
sampling_model.units: The canonical observed record lies in \(\mathsf H_B=(\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\) with its product Borel sigma-algebra. The law is built recursively by appending a randomized assignment vector and then independent Gaussian responses from the assigned-arm kernels; no joint coupling of unobserved arm outcomes is posited.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with every realized batch share constrained to \([1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.overlap: Pathwise exact-count overlap: \(\lceil m_b/4\rceil\le q_b(h)\le\lfloor3m_b/4\rfloor\) for every canonical prefix \(h\in\mathsf H_{b-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Arm variances are learned from deterministic prefixes of each observed arm stream and projected onto \([\ell^2,u^2]\); no random-size chi-square assertion is used.

body.tldr: Policy updates are a scarce experimental-design resource, but requiring updates and merely allowing them have different frontiers. The exactly-\(B\) normalized excess MSE has three regimes: the chronological term \(B\{(n+1)^{1/B}-1\}/n\) for \(B\leq\log(n+1)\), a \(\log(n+1)/n\) plateau through \(B\asymp\sqrt{n\log n}\), and compulsory-batching loss \((B/n)^2\) thereafter. The at-most-\(B\) envelope reaches order \((\log n)/n\) after order \(\log n\) useful updates, while the exact-batch harm becomes rate-dominant only at the later square-root elbow. A deterministic-prefix plug-in design matches the frontier up to constants and supports a uniformly valid fixed-time Wald interval. The sharp chronological constant and the literal factor-two saturation threshold remain open.

project_justification.gap: Existing adaptive Neyman results provide first-order efficiency, fixed-stage upper rates, unrestricted lower bounds, or low-switching constructions, but do not give a matched actual-MSE phase diagram for every required exact update count with integer allocations and deterministic batch-contrast weights. In particular, they do not separate useful-update saturation near \(\log n\) from compulsory-batching dominance near \(\sqrt{n\log n}\).
project_justification.niche: The exact-count chronological design has two distinct losses. Delayed variance learning controls the frontier until it plateaus at order \(\log(n+1)/n\), whereas the per-batch treatment-count lattice contributes \((B/n)^2\) and becomes dominant only beyond the square-root elbow. The at-most budget can stop at the earlier elbow; an exactly-\(B\) policy cannot discard compulsory batches.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the risk decomposition and the matching every-\(B\) frontier, derives its three integer-indexed regimes directly, characterizes the at-most envelope and large-constant operational-factor saturation, retains the \(1/3\) maximum-batching witness, and attaches studentized fixed-time inference to a matching deterministic-prefix design. It does not infer the literal factor-two threshold from order bounds.

body.related_work: Li and Simchi-Levi give low-update constructions and characterize sequential efficiency through average propensity; their timing-collapsed benchmark does not furnish the present every-required-update phase diagram. Zhao derives fixed-stage competitive upper exponents and an unrestricted adaptive proxy-risk lower bound, whereas the present result concerns actual weighted-estimator MSE under a fixed exactly-\(B\) chronological decision class. Hirano and Porter's endogenous-information-set representation motivates the local chronological experiment, and Armstrong's adaptive efficiency bound supplies a first-order least-favorable-score template. Batched-bandit grids and feedback-gap arguments of Perchet, Rigollet, Chassang, and Snowberg and of Gao, Han, Ren, and Zhou inform the construction under a different reward-regret loss. Cai and Rafi and Yamin motivate compact-interior pilot comparisons; Wright isolates static integer-allocation loss; and Blackwell, Pashley, and Valentino motivate volume-weighted exact-count batch contrasts. No theorem-level transfer to Li--Simchi-Levi's or Zhao's full design games is claimed. A Gaussian parameter-submodel converse can transfer upward to a larger outcome-law class only when the admissible decision class and the risk functional are held fixed. The public Amazon adaptive-abtester is the operational cadence consumer, not evidence for the mathematical lower bound.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-scale path in \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{LAN}}\) holds \(s\) fixed. If common scale is allowed to vary as an unknown nuisance along the local path, the efficient information for the variance-ratio parameter depends on the treated and control counts, so the information-two calculation cannot be imported unchanged. The sharp-constant analysis must preserve this distinction.
body.honest_scope: The proved claims are the two-sided every-\(B\) order frontier, its three-regime exact-batch phase diagram, the at-most envelope, saturation at order \(\log n\) for a sufficiently large fixed comparison factor, the exact one-batch formula, the two-batch exponent, the \(1/3\) maximum-batching witness, and uniform fixed-time Wald coverage for the constructed design. Useful-update saturation occurs at order \(\log n\), while compulsory exact-batching loss becomes rate-dominant only at order \(\sqrt{n\log n}\). The exact leading constant of \(\Psi_\infty(n)\), a uniformly matching sharp schedule, the exact finite-sample two-batch minimax rule, and the literal factor-two saturation threshold remain open. No result is claimed for a comparator's broader design or risk game merely because its outcome-law class contains the Gaussian submodel.
